**JIRA Ticket:**
[BFD-3115](https://jira.cms.gov/browse/BFD-3115)

**User Story or Bug Summary:**

<!-- Please copy-paste the brief user story or bug description that this PR is intended to address. -->

As a Peering Partner, I want a simple and automatable mechanism to send files via the CMS EFT process so that I can enable my processes relying on that file transfer without needing to worry about the finer details

---

### What Does This PR Do?

<!--
Add detailed description & discussion of changes here.
The contents of this section should be used as your commit message (unless you merge the PR via a merge commit, of course).

Please follow standard Git commit message guidelines:
* First line should be a capitalized, short (50 chars or less) summary.
* The rest of the message should be in standard Markdown format, wrapped to 72 characters.
* Describe your changes in imperative mood, e.g. "make xyzzy do frotz" instead of "[This patch] makes xyzzy do frotz" or "[I] changed xyzzy to do frotz", as if you are giving orders to the codebase to change its behavior.
* List all relevant Jira issue keys, one per line at the end of the message, per: <https://confluence.atlassian.com/jirasoftwarecloud/processing-issues-with-smart-commits-788960027.html>.

Reference: <https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Distributed-Git-Contributing-to-a-Project>.
-->

This PR implements BFD EFT Outbound using a Lambda function invoked by S3 Event Notifications that will, based off configured "recognized file" patterns, send files uploaded to partner-specific outbound subfolders in the BFD EFT Bucket to the appropriate destination on the configured CMS EFT SFTP server. In short, the process looks like this:

- A Peering Partner uploads a recognized file (a file matching a filename pattern and destination folder configured in SSM) to their corresponding "pending" file directory in the BFD EFT S3 Bucket
- An S3 Event Notification is generated, and invokes the outbound Lambda
- The Outbound Lambda picks up the file, and sends it via SFTP to its configured destination folder
- The file is moved from the partner's "pending" folder to their "sent" folder (which, if configured, will send S3 Event Notifications to notify of this success)
  - If this process fails, then the Lambda moves the file to the partner's "failed" directory under a sub-folder that generally indicates _what_ failed when trying to upload the file (similar to the "sent" folder, notification targets can be configured to receive S3 Notifications when files land in this "failed" directory as well)

To support this:

- The `eft` Terraservice and its corresponding configuration have been refactored significantly
- The new Lambda requires an external dependency for SFTP, [`paramiko`](https://www.paramiko.org/). This library appears to be _widely_ used and is well-supported
- The new Lambda, as it requires an external dependency, is a _Docker-based_ Lambda.
  - The Lambda's corresponding image is generated by a new Jenkins pipeline, `bfd-build-eft-sftp-outbound-transfer-lambda`.
  - This new Pipeline has already been created and used to generate the Docker image during testing. **It will need to be updated to target `master` when these changes are merged**
  - The Docker image is tagged based off of BFD's latest release version, and is uploaded to a private ECR repository when built

Additionally, AB2D's `test` configuration has been included ahead-of-time in this PR, rather than encoding their configuration in the existing form and needing to update it when this PR is merged.

These changes have been verified by:

- `terraform apply`ing `eft` and `base` to `test`, using a fake partner named `testing`, **verifying that** everything is applied as expected and all resources are correct
- Defining a mock "recognized file" with the filename pattern `^X\.TST\.A\d+\.XYZ12\.D\d+\.T\d+$` with a destination of `/3115_test/success`, configuring the outbound target SFTP server to point to the existing SFTP Transfer Family server running for `test` EFT, and then uploading a ~250 MB file to the pending outbound directory in the S3 Bucket, **verifying that** the Outbound Lambda was able to transfer the file over SFTP to the correct destination _and_ that the file was moved to the "sent" directory in `testing`'s home path
- Configuring AB2D's `dev` information for _inbound_, and with the assistance of AB2D, **verifying that** AB2D was able to receive S3 Event Notifications using these changes and that they were able to assume the generated role and manipulate files within this sub-folder (and nowhere else)

body:
I have looked into adding stoichiometric coefficients following discussions in #513. It turns out there was already a coefficient assigned in `src/inputFunctions.f90` for each species in each reaction, it was just being set to 1 every time. This coefficient of 1 was then already included in calculations in the `resid` subroutine in `src/solverFunctions.f90`. This made it fairly easy to modify the code to have variable coefficients!

I have made the following adjustments:
- Check for stoichiometric coefficients when reading the species (reactants and products) in each reaction in `build/mech_converter.py`. If no coefficient is given then assign a coefficient of 1.
- Carry these coefficients through as a new column in the files `mechanism.reac` and `mechanism.prod`.
- Read the coefficients in  `src/inputFunctions.f90` instead of assigning a value of 1 for all species.

I've run some models to test this and it seems to be behaving well. I've compared against the previous version with species duplicated and the results are identical. I've also tested some edge-cases like setting the coefficient to 0 and non-integer reactant coefficients, which also work as intended.

Let me know if there's any more changes I need to make, otherwise this resolves #513.

author: fbrausse
body:
Writing to const-qualified global symbols is not allowed by C. Related: #1548. `memset` is special, though, since it doesn't use a WRITE derefence, but an INTERNAL one. I'm still thinking how to solve this. Either replicate the const-check there, or - what I think might be more useful: separate the "internal" flag from read/write in the dereference mode. Not sure. For now, this fixes writes to const globals except intrinsic_memset().

I'll add some test cases showing this later. Maybe after xmas, we'll see.

Fixes #870

#### Purpose of change
PR #68582 pruned a little too aggressively around what qualified for various martial arts. Many of those changes were justified when it involved fencing, but did not make sense when involving HEMA-similar styles. I discussed this in #70110
<!-- With a few sentences, describe your reasons for making this change.

#### Describe the solution
This re-adds a few missing tags to the early wooden swords. It also removes the club tag from the wooden greatsword, as the balance would be entirely wrong to work as a club.
<!-- How does the feature work, or how does this fix a bug?  The easier you make your solution to understand, the faster it can get merged. -->

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
One could delete the swords entirely, since they have no purpose seperate from clubs if they cannot be used by medieval martial arts. But this is unrealistic in the extreme, since the weight and balance of such swords is meant to mimic a real weapon, and thus while they would lack damage, they would perform as a fine substitute.
<!-- Explain any alternative solutions, different approaches, or possibilities you've considered using to solve the same problem. -->

Loaded the game, spawned the various swords, confirmed that they work with the proper martial art.

I'm not entirely sure a 'nord' should exist, since driving a ton of nails into a wooden sword would probably just make it prone to breaking easily. But I can't find anything about nords in real life, so I felt it was beyond my knowledge to say they ought not to work at all.

author: idpaterson
body:
Balance and transaction exports continue to run in the background when the popup is closed or the back button is clicked as long as Mint is still open. However, the download buttons that you see on the main popup screen clear the existing state and start a new export. Now we have two balance exports running simultaneously and the progress bar jumps erratically between the first and second export job progress.

This pull request simply shows the progress screen for those download tasks if a job is already running. Since it is possible for a job to get hung up and never finish the extension will show the error screen after a certain period of inactivity. There is probably a more idiomatic way to accomplish that than a `setTimeout()`, but it works.

The "abandoned job" state can be tested easily with the unpacked extension. 
1. Start an export for all account balance history
2. Go to `chrome://extensions` in a separate tab
3. Press the reload button next to the extension which will kill the service worker but not reset the state
4. Open the popup and wait for the error screen to appear
